# Relay: wave 2 PostgreSQL cutover (dev)

**Started:** 2026-08-24
**Status:** planning

## Objective

Wave 2 of the DynamoDB to PostgreSQL migration is live in the dev environment:
catalog.agents, catalog.agent_groups and iam.user_groups are read AND written
through PostgreSQL, agent administration works end to end against it, and a real
Cortex chat succeeds using a credential resolved from Secrets Manager. Rollback
to DynamoDB has been rehearsed and its data cost is known and written down.

## Constraints

- Dev only. Prod has no PostgreSQL instance and is entirely out of scope: no prod
  gitops values, no prod database, no prod secrets. Stage is provisioned but empty
  and is not part of this relay.
- Zero comments and zero docstrings in code written. Intent lives in names.
- No workarounds, bypass flags, hardcoding or deferred fixes. Root cause only.
- Never push to develop, stage or main. Feature branches and MRs only, each with
  a real description.
- No .md files, progress logs or scratchpads committed to the code repo.
  Documentation goes in GitLab issues and MR descriptions.
- Tests assert behaviour, never mirror the implementation, and are mutation
  checked. A test that still passes when its guard is deleted is worthless; this
  project has been burned by that repeatedly.
- Local gate before any push: ruff, black, isort, pytest. Baseline is 1232 passed
  and 5 failed. Those 5 are tests/db/test_backend_selection.py failing only
  because the local venv lacks psycopg. Do not fix them and do not let the
  failure count grow.
- Python: services/agent-service/.venv/bin/python, run from services/agent-service.

## Non-goals

- Waves 3, 4, 5 and 6.
- Stage and prod cutover.
- Minting the two missing agent PATs. The relay cannot create credentials.
- Fixing the security findings already tracked against
  fix/agents-router-authentication, including the /api/v1/chat entitlement gap
  recorded as issue #1.
- Any change to the DynamoDB code path beyond what substitutability requires.

## Decisions log

| Date | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-24 | Branch wave 2 off fix/agents-router-authentication, not develop | PgAgentRepository._select() must return guest_access_enabled, and AgentItem.guestAccessEnabled exists only on that branch. Branching off develop would require a follow-up leg gated on the security merge, and if wave 2 cut over first every agent would read guest-disabled and unwritable once security landed. One place, no ordering trap. Cost accepted: wave 2 cannot merge until the security branch does. |
| 2026-08-24 | Cut over with 5 of 7 agents credentialled | agent-ec00bc8c (Project Governance AI) and agent-ee6950bd (TPMO AI Assistance) have no PAT in either store. They are broken today, before any migration. Cutover neither causes nor worsens it. Accepted as debt; the contract must prove cutover changed nothing for them rather than quietly leaving them failing. |
| 2026-08-24 | Reconciliation happens on a NEW branch feat/wave2-cutover-reconciled, cut from feature/non-prod-wave2-cutover | The 22-commit original stays intact as a fallback. If reconciliation goes wrong the answer is to delete a branch, not to unpick a merge. |
| 2026-08-24 | S1 cleared with Finding 1 already closed by a later leg | The code judge, correctly pinned to the S1 tip, found develop's credential guard inert on PostgreSQL. The credential-parity leg had already fixed exactly that; verified on the current branch - blank, bullet and asterisk masks are all dropped with a warning while a real PAT passes. Recorded rather than re-opened. |
| 2026-08-24 | S2 cleared on the round-2 CODE judge plus coach verification, without a round-2 behaviour judge | The round-1 behaviour judge drove the product hard - 195 self-written probes across four chat mounts - and found no authorization bypass; its only failure was ACC-CRED-004. The fix round touched the shared predicate and tests, nothing in the routing or ownership paths it had cleared. The round-2 code judge then drove HTTP itself and confirmed the agentType Custom bypass closed, built a 28-shape decision table through BOTH guards showing zero disagreements, and re-applied all four previously-survivable mutations. Re-running a full behaviour judge would re-test surfaces nothing had touched. Recording the judgement because it is a deliberate reduction in rigour, not an oversight. |
| 2026-08-24 | S3 re-sequenced: merging to develop is a hard prerequisite, not an optional finish | Migrations reach dev only through a pinned container image run as an ArgoCD PostSync hook. The db-schema image builds ONLY on develop or db-PostgreSQL; feat/wave2-cutover-reconciled builds nothing, and all 26 published tags were resolved SHA-to-tree with none containing 0003. So the sequence is merge, build, hand-bump the db-migrate pin, sync, verify. The old apply-migration-0003 leg assumed dev could be migrated directly and was replaced. |
| 2026-08-24 | Facilities F&Q is the cutover canary; no per-agent routing is built | Owner asked to cut over one agent first. Wave 2 cannot be partitioned by agent: iam.user_groups has columns id, legacy_id, user_id, group_id, role, created_at, updated_at - no agent dimension at all - and auth-service reads the same repository to derive agent_manager at login, so a per-agent switch in agent-service alone would leave the two services disagreeing about where membership lives and agent_manager silently wrong after re-login. Instead the canary is the verification order, backed by a field-by-field parity check proving Facilities is clean and unaffected by the read-path gap. |
| 2026-08-24 | The relay performs the dev cutover and verifies it | Owner chose flip-and-verify over hand-off. The flag flip is the last leg and is gated on evidence from every preceding check, never on assumption. |

## Dismissed items

| Item | From leg | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| develop's merged-in code carries docstrings, not stripped | reconcile-develop | Correct call by the runner. The zero-comments rule governs code the relay writes, not commits authored elsewhere that arrive through a merge. Stripping them would rewrite someone else's work inside a merge commit and make the diff unreviewable. |
| Branch left local, not pushed | reconcile-develop | Correct call. Pushing an intermediate reconciliation leg would start a CI pipeline on a tree no judge has seen. The first leg that needs a remote ref pushes it. |
| services/db-schema tests appear to run in no suite | reconcile-security | Dismissed with evidence. The CI job `db-schema-test` runs `pytest tests/` with `PGTEST_REQUIRED=1` against a real postgres:16-alpine service, after a full upgrade/idempotency/downgrade cycle. The gap is local only: the agent-service venv lacks psycopg and db-schema is outside its testpaths. Recorded in the test-suite skill instead of spending a leg. |
| PgAgentRepository does not select guest_access_enabled | reconcile-security | Not dismissed - already claimed by leg `read-path-columns` as ACC-PARITY-002 and ACC-PARITY-003. Correctly left alone by this runner. |
| _store_credential coerces a non-string credential; one existing test pins that | credential-parity | Dismissed. The shared rule governs strings because masking is a string phenomenon. A numeric value is not a mask, and both backends retain it identically, so the two still agree - which is what ACC-CRED-004 actually requires. Rewriting that test would change behaviour no check asks for. |
| by-database-schema 404 echoes the caller's own database/schema | behaviour-judge-S1 | Dismissed as a leak. The caller supplied both values, and the "no such agent" and "not entitled" branches return an identical message, so there is no enumeration oracle. Normalising it to a constant is cosmetic and would touch a file two later legs already own. |
| Chat body validation returns 422 before the entitlement 404 | behaviour-judge-S1 | Dismissed. Authentication runs and passes first (anonymous with the same malformed body is 401) and the 422 names only the caller's own missing field. Validation-before-authorization is FastAPI's ordering, not a defect. |
| HEAD /agents/{id} returns 405 rather than 401 | behaviour-judge-S1 | Dismissed. Routes declare GET only, the refusal carries no body, and nothing leaks. Worth knowing that the security suite's route sweep excludes HEAD, which is recorded here rather than spent as a leg. |
| GET / is unauthenticated and returns name, version, feature list | behaviour-judge-S1 | Dismissed. A public service banner by design, and the only 2xx an anonymous caller obtained anywhere in the application. |
| get_current_admin is strict-admin, so agent_manager cannot reach /agents mutations | behaviour-judge-S1 | Not dismissed and not a leg. This is an RBAC product question - whether managers should operate agents - and is outside a database migration relay. Raised to the owner instead. |
| Five test assertions using != 403 / not in REJECTED | code-judge-S1 | Dismissed with evidence. All five are negative controls ("an admin is not blocked") and the load-bearing deny assertions beside them use == 403. The judge probed the live app and confirmed none is currently masking a 500. tests/security itself is clean. |
| Seven unused auth helpers and two aliases attached to zero routes | code-judge-S1 | Dismissed. Dead surface, not a defect, and deleting it would touch files three later legs own. Recorded so nobody mistakes the "use these in new routes" comment for guidance that was followed. |
| Infrastructure failures laundered into 404s | code-judge-S1 | Not dismissed, not a leg. admin_db_service swallows every exception and returns None, so a datastore outage makes every non-admin see 404 on every agent route, indistinguishable from a permission denial and invisible to alerting. Already raised by the earlier operational review as a pre-deploy detection requirement. Raised to the owner rather than fixed inside a migration relay. |
| No lock_timeout anywhere on the migration path | migration research | Not dismissed, not a leg. ADD COLUMN with a non-volatile default is metadata-only on PG 16.1 (version confirmed from the running container), so the lock is held sub-millisecond. The risk is lock ACQUISITION: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE queues behind any in-flight transaction on catalog.agents and everything queues behind it, with only activeDeadlineSeconds 600 as a ceiling. Worth a PGOPTIONS lock_timeout hardening later; raised to the owner rather than changed mid-relay. |
| db-migrate and agent-service are separate ArgoCD Applications with no ordering | migration research | Not dismissed. Converted into a load-bearing boundary on deploy-and-soak instead: a failed migration does not stop the app rolling out, and once read-path-columns makes the app SELECT guest_access_enabled, deploying the image before the migration means querying a column that does not exist. |
| Stage db-migrate may be drifted | migration research | Dismissed for this relay. Stage is explicitly a non-goal; the observation is recorded so nobody assumes stage reflects the current chart. |
| create_teams_channel writes Teams channels into the agents table | create-path-credential-guard | Not dismissed and not fixed here. Raised to the owner: earlier research recorded the Teams tables as dead surface awaiting D11 deletion. If Teams is live, this needs its own leg because cutover turns a silent failure into a 500. If it is dead surface, it should be deleted rather than repaired. Attached to cutover-verify as a known behaviour change either way. |
| QueueService is missing add_message_job, get_job_status and add_batch_job | process-entitlement | Not dismissed, raised to the owner. /process/ with stream:true, /process/job/{id} and /process/batch therefore 500 on every call, and require_job_owner is dead code today. Only the non-streaming POST /process/ is live - which is precisely the path that was exploitable, so the fix still mattered. Repairing the queue is a behaviour change beyond a migration relay. |
| Legacy roles:["admin"] now counts as admin in require_job_owner | process-entitlement | Accepted, not dismissed. A real semantic delta from consolidating onto is_admin_claim, but it matches admin_auth.require_admin, so it makes two paths agree rather than introducing a new rule. |
| pg-tests-run-in-ci closed by inspection, no code written | coach | The leg existed because research reported agent-service had no CI job for tests/pg. That was true of develop and false of the reconciled branch, which carries pg-integration-test: it upgrades the database to alembic head, then runs both services' tests/pg with PGTEST_REQUIRED=1, and agent-service's conftest raises rather than skipping when that flag is set. Closing on evidence rather than spending a leg is the correct outcome, but it is a reminder that research read against the wrong branch produces phantom work. |
| SessionClient and the published session-service spec disagree | chat-session-ownership | Raised to the owner, not fixed. The spec returns {"success","session"} with no messages key and uses POST for messages; the client reads session["messages"] and uses PUT. If the spec is authoritative, get_session_messages has ALWAYS returned [] and chat has never had conversational memory. That is a product-behaviour question well outside a migration relay, and the ownership guard reads the owner from either shape so it holds regardless. |
| session-service enforces no ownership on any endpoint this client uses | chat-session-ownership | Raised to the owner. It is open to any caller on the network; agent-service can only guarantee its own boundary, which this leg now does. Fixing the service itself is outside this repo. |
| M10 (empty or non-string user_id) survives mutation | chat-session-ownership | Accepted. The runner declined to manufacture a test for it because such a requester is refused one branch earlier, so the case is unreachable by construction. Not writing a vacuous test is the right call. |
| The queue_name cutover story in my briefings was WRONG | pg-repository-correctness | Correcting the record. Research inferred from the repository's _select() omission without checking the downstream consumer. src/config/agents.py:72-95 rebuilds every agent at boot as a hand-listed dict that drops all eight tuning fields BEFORE conversion, so engineering_ai gets queue_name="default" under DynamoDB TODAY. It is pre-existing on both backends, NOT a cutover regression, and therefore not a cutover blocker. Raised to the owner: fixing it changes live RQ queue routing on the DynamoDB path, which is a product decision, not a migration one. |
| Runner reported tests/pg never runs in CI for agent-service | pg-repository-correctness | Dismissed, runner mistaken. Re-verified: job pg-integration-test runs agent-service tests/pg at its lines 45-49 with PGTEST_REQUIRED=1, on both merge_request_event and push, against a database upgraded to alembic head earlier in the same job. The runner most likely read testpaths in pytest.ini, which CI overrides by passing the path explicitly. |
| SQL injection surface in snowflake_sdk_service.py:125-135 | thread-id-ownership | RAISED TO THE OWNER, not fixed. The query f-string interpolates thread_id AND agent_name directly, and puts json.dumps(messages) inside a single-quoted SQL literal. routers/chat.py:158 feeds thread_id from request.context.get(), an untyped dict, so a string reaches it. Mitigating: USE_SNOWFLAKE_SDK is unset in dev, stage and prod values and unset on the live dev pod, so the REST path is what runs - this code is dormant. Not a migration concern and not a cutover blocker, but it is a live injection vector the moment that toggle is turned on. |
| Chat now has a read-after-write dependency on session-service persisting thread_id | thread-id-ownership | Accepted, and flagged for the cutover checks. If that PUT silently fails or the GET omits the field, a caller's own next turn 404s. Fail-closed and correct, but it must be exercised against a live session-service before this is trusted in production. |
| Thread ids are timestamp-derived and not namespaced per agent | thread-id-ownership | Accepted as debt. Guessability is what made the defect exploitable; the ownership guard closes the exploit without needing the ids to be unguessable. Renaming the id scheme is a data-format change well outside this relay. |
| POST /chat in dynamic_chat.py has the identical thread defect | thread-id-ownership | Not dismissed. It scopes by conversation rather than session, so the guard does not transfer as written. Added to GitLab issue #1, which already tracks that router's missing entitlement and which the owner has deferred. |
| config/agents.py rebuilds every agent from a key list that drops all eight tuning settings | s2-test-quality | RAISED TO THE OWNER, pinned not fixed. Third reviewer to reach it and the first to prove it end to end: every agent in the live registry runs on AgentConfig defaults - queue_name "default", max_threads 100, rate_limit_per_minute 60 - regardless of what is stored, on BOTH backends. The repository round trip is now correct; the loss is entirely in that rebuild. Fixing it changes live RQ queue routing on the DynamoDB path, which is a product decision. An xfail(strict=True) test drives the real boot path so it turns red the moment someone fixes it, rather than sitting as a comment nobody reads. |
| pat*with*stars*inside is the only thing forcing proportion over a zero-mask rule | mask-shape-coverage | Raised to the owner, deliberately not resolved by the runner. A stricter "any mask character disqualifies" rule would also catch bullets-plus-eight-characters, but it refuses any credential containing an asterisk, and an existing test asserts that shape IS real. Mutation M5 showed the strict rule breaking 8 assertions - that is an admin locked out of rotating a PAT, which is worse than the residual risk. Proportion was the right call on the evidence available; if the product says an asterisk can never appear in a PAT, the stricter rule becomes available. |
| admin_db_service still exposes _is_a_real_credential as a second NAME for the shared predicate | mask-shape-coverage | Accepted. It delegates, and a test proves the delegation, so it is not a second rule. Recorded because a future edit could fork it - which is exactly how the two credential paths diverged originally. |
| The majority rule accepts 15 ASCII mask shapes and short partial reveals | code-judge-S2 round 2 | RAISED TO THE OWNER. Not a regression - the previous rule accepted them too - and all three masks the contract names are refused. But `########`, `xxxxxxxx`, `REDACTED`, `null` and short reveals like `***3f9a` still read as real credentials and would overwrite a stored PAT. The rule catches a partial reveal only when the mask portion is at least half, so it is a threshold rather than a catch, and the commit message overstates that. The production admin UI is not in this repo, so which mask it actually sends is unknown - that is the fact needed to decide whether to tighten further. |
| The tightening widened an existing credential-DESTROYING branch | code-judge-S2 round 2 | RAISED TO THE OWNER. admin_db_service.py:560-563 pops the stored PAT rather than preserving it when the STORED value itself fails the predicate. With a stored value like 'a*b*c*', a masked save returns 200 and silently drops the credential. Low practical risk, silent when it fires. Pre-existing branch, newly reachable for a few more stored shapes. |
| Three stale prunable worktrees registered on this repo | reconcile-develop | Housekeeping unrelated to the relay; cleaned by the coach rather than spending a leg on it. |
